hackathon_llama32_1b_LEVER2_CACHELINE_ST._doc: ROOT-CAUSE DIAGNOSIS of a severe, real board regression from PR#169's board run (2026-07-23T20:08Z, run 30038575018). Lever 2 (cache-line-owned atomic-free output stores, independently implemented this session on both PR#168 and PR#169) has a fundamental parallelism bug, distinct from and much more serious than a correctness issue -- it passed the oracle (test-backend-ops, small m=16 shapes) because the oracle's tiny test shapes don't expose it, but is catastrophic at real model scale.
hackathon_llama32_1b_LEVER2_CACHELINE_ST.the_bug: Original hart striping for the M (output row) dimension is `for (m = hart_id; m < M; m += stride_m)` with stride_m=2048 (the total hart count). For M=2048 (Llama-3.2-1B's hidden_size), this is a perfect 1:1 mapping -- all 2048 harts active, each computing exactly one output row. Lever 2's restructured striping was `for (line = hart_id; line < M_lines; line += stride_m)` where M_lines = M >> 4 = 128 (number of 16-row/64B cache lines). Since stride_m (2048) was left unchanged but the loop bound (M_lines) shrank 16x, only harts 0-127 ever execute the loop body -- the other 1920 harts are completely idle -- while the 128 active harts each sequentially compute all 16 rows in their line (a for-j-in-0..16 inner loop) instead of 1. Total work is conserved; active hardware parallelism collapsed from 2048-way to 128-way, a 16x reduction in units doing work simultaneously.
hackathon_llama32_1b_LEVER2_CACHELINE_ST.real_board_evidence: PR#169 board run (mask-hoist + Lever2 cache-line-stores + Lever3 scale-unpack, run 30038575018): llama32_1b candidate 4.7086 tok/s vs paired baseline 13.4644 tok/s (baseline itself was healthy/normal this run, ruling out board degradation as the cause) -- a ~2.86x slowdown. ALL 11 OTHER shared regression models ALSO collapsed by a similar ~60-70% simultaneously (lfm25 2.3774 vs required>=3.0896, gemma3n_e2b 1.1085 vs >=2.0899, tinyllama11b 4.3577 vs >=12.3390, smollm2_135m 7.1543 vs >=12.3580, etc.) -- fully consistent with the bug being IN THE SHARED mul_mat_Q8_0.c file every one of these Q8_0-quantized models dispatches through, not board contention (which would show a milder, more variable pattern like the ~5-25% dip seen earlier this session, not a uniform ~60-70% collapse across every model at once).
hackathon_llama32_1b_LEVER2_CACHELINE_ST.why_the_2.86x_observed_is_less_than_the_: The kernel is memory-bandwidth-bound for the N=1 decode case (per ChiruGuru99's own real profiling comment, found earlier this session: 'mul_mat_Q8_0 is ~76% of firmware cycles AND memory-bound... atomic_store_f32 [contention] implicated as the shared bottleneck'). With fewer active harts issuing DRAM requests, there is less request-level parallelism to hide memory latency, but the memory system's own internal request overlap absorbs SOME of the theoretical 16x loss -- landing at an observed ~2.86x rather than the naive 16x. The DIRECTION and rough magnitude are exactly what this bug predicts; this is not attributed to noise.
hackathon_llama32_1b_LEVER2_CACHELINE_ST.why_the_oracle_did_not_catch_it: test-backend-ops's default MUL_MAT sweep only exercises m=16 (M_lines=1) -- with only 1 cache line total, the 'only 128 of 2048 harts active' failure mode is invisible (there's only 1 unit of work regardless of striping scheme at that trivial scale). The bug ONLY manifests at real model scale (M=2048 -> 128 lines, vastly fewer than the 2048 available harts). LESSON: correctness oracles verifying tiny/edge-case shapes do not substitute for a REAL-SCALE performance check; a change that only alters PARALLELISM STRUCTURE (not the math) can pass every correctness oracle case and still be catastrophically wrong at production scale. Any future hart-striping change needs a real-scale board or profiled check, not just a small-shape correctness pass.
hackathon_llama32_1b_LEVER2_CACHELINE_ST.retroactive_reframing_of_ChiruGuru99s_ow: ChiruGuru99's own more-advanced fork (read earlier this session) had a structurally IDENTICAL cache-line-ownership idea (one hart per 64B line, for j in 0..16 sequential rows) and disabled it via a hardcoded `aligned = false`, calling it merely 'unsafe' without diagnosing why in their commit message. Given this session independently rediscovered the exact same design and found it causes a severe REAL performance regression (not just a correctness edge case), it is now plausible -- though not proven, since we don't have their internal reasoning -- that this same parallelism collapse (not only a correctness bug) is why they disabled it rather than fix it. This corpus entry is what should have existed BEFORE re-deriving the same design blind.
hackathon_llama32_1b_LEVER2_CACHELINE_ST.the_real_fix_needed_for_cache_line_owner: To remove the atomic-store bottleneck WITHOUT collapsing parallelism, the correct design needs to preserve full one-hart-per-row assignment (so all 2048 harts stay active, each still computing exactly one row) while having GROUPS of 16 harts that happen to share a destination cache line cooperate via a barrier/synchronization primitive to jointly publish one combined 64B store, instead of each hart storing its own element atomically. This requires real inter-hart synchronization (a barrier or shared-flag protocol across the 16 harts in a group) which is a materially bigger and riskier undertaking than the naive 'one hart owns the whole line sequentially' version built this session. NOT attempted this session given the risk/time tradeoff -- flagged here as the actual correct direction for a future attempt, not something to blindly retry.
hackathon_llama32_1b_LEVER2_CACHELINE_ST.decision_taken: Lever 2 (cache-line-owned stores, as implemented) is being REVERTED on both PR#168 and PR#169 -- reverting to the original per-element atomic-store striping (which, while it does pay the atomic contention cost ChiruGuru99's profiling identified, at least preserves full 2048-way parallelism and is the PROVEN, board-measured-safe baseline mask-hoist already used). Lever 3 (vectorized fp16 scale-unpack) is architecturally independent of hart striping -- it only changes how a SINGLE hart's OWN row computation converts block scales, with no cross-hart interaction -- and is being kept and re-verified alone, since there is no structural reason to expect it shares this bug.

This is direct, real-hardware confirmation that reverting the hart-striping change fixed the actual regression, not just a hypothesis.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PARALLELISM_FIX_CON.residual_pattern_this_run_9_of_11_regres: gemma3n_e2b 1.5724 vs required 2.0899 (~25% short), tinyllama11b 11.2042 vs 12.3390 (~9% short), smollm2_135m/360m/17b each ~7-9% short, rwkv7_15b ~8% short (+ppl issue), qwen25_05b ~8.6% short, deepseek_r1_15b ~10% short, smolvlm_256m ~8% short -- while lfm25 (99.3% of reference, within the 1% regression tolerance -- PASS) and qwen3_8b (102.2% of reference -- PASS) came through clean. A ~7-10% mild, INCONSISTENT shortfall across most-but-not-all shared models (not the uniform ~60-70% collapse the real bug caused) does not fit a code-caused regression from scale-unpack (which is architecturally confined to a single hart's own row computation, same reasoning as before) -- it fits board-level contention instead.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PARALLELISM_FIX_CON.PR171_AFOliveira_board_migration_IN_PROG: aifoundry-org/hf-hackathon PR#171 (open, maintainer AFOliveira): 'ci: migrate ET board benchmarks to aifoundry3' -- moves ALL trusted workflows to a new, hardware-epoch-pinned runner (et-soc1-aifoundry3-600-400-tdp0-v1), enforces board/clock/TDP provenance stamped into every score, and CRITICALLY 'harden[s] llama.cpp revision and runtime-library provenance' -- a direct fix for the exact 'candidate score does not identify the exact PR head commit' bug that has appeared on EVERY one of our own runs today (and historically on PR#91/#111 per corpus entries from 2026-07-15/16). PR description explicitly states validation included 'post-power-cycle aifoundry3 smoke and repeated stability runs' -- i.e. the maintainer is actively power-cycling and stress-testing the shared board infrastructure concurrently with our own gate runs. After merge, the leaderboard gets bootstrapped fresh for all 16 models.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PARALLELISM_FIX_CON.why_this_matters_for_strategy: The mild, inconsistent ~7-10% shortfall pattern this run is very plausibly contention from AFOliveira's own concurrent migration/stability testing on the shared board, not evidence our scale-unpack lever is unsafe -- but this can't be fully disentangled from a small real effect without a clean run. Given (a) our own target metric (llama32_1b) came back cleanly in the normal noise band, (b) the persistent provenance bug on our own row is explicitly being fixed by #171, and (c) hammering the board for more data points right now measures instability we can't control or attribute cleanly: the disciplined choice is to STOP further board iteration until PR#171 merges, then get a clean, stable, provenance-correct read on our actual candidate. This is a deliberate patience call, not inaction -- matches the same 'stop pushing, verify infrastructure health before trusting a result' discipline already learned earlier this session (docker-oracle transient failures, board-degradation-from-repeated-runs).

hackathon_llama32_1b_REHAN_PERMISSION_an._doc: MAJOR STRATEGY SHIFT, 2026-07-23. Ryan reported RehanQasim-dev (current #1, 14.7096 tok/s) gave explicit permission (direct message) to use/build on his code, superseding the standing feedback_hackathon_no_copying_competitor_code caution for this specific case. This entry documents the resulting lever-overlap analysis before any code was adopted.
hackathon_llama32_1b_REHAN_PERMISSION_an.authorization: Ryan's direct instruction: 'that rule is now gone and rehan has given blessing to me in message, the idea is to put forward the best overall run period, so we pull all these levers, figure out the overlap and then apply what really works.' This is Ryan's call to make as the account owner acting on reported real-world permission from the code's actual author -- not an inference or assumption on this session's part.
hackathon_llama32_1b_REHAN_PERMISSION_an.critical_finding_our_levers_are_redundan: Read block_ops.h from RehanQasim's own authored commit (84405bb7f86458c60c9f47a6a140f1c876da8532, 'et-backend: Q8_0 matrix-engine GEMM kernel for prefill', 2026-07-14) directly. His q8_dot_compute/q8_dot_tile/q8_dot_reduce family ALREADY implements every technique our two proven levers deliver, in a more complete form: (1) mask-hoist -- q8_dot_begin/end split-phase API, identical concept to ours; (2) row-vector-accumulate -- f20 persists as the row accumulator across the WHOLE row (reset once, accumulated per block via q8_dot_tile, reduced ONCE via q8_dot_reduce) -- the exact 'Lever 1' we deprioritized earlier from ChiruGuru99's code, already present here; (3) hardware fp16 scale-convert -- uses fbcx.ps (broadcast scalar to vector) + fcvt.ps.f16 (hardware convert) INSTEAD OF fp16_to_fp32()'s scalar branchy convert, done PER-BLOCK (not batched-8 like our scale-unpack lever, but still avoids the exact branchy scalar path we were targeting). PLUS things we never built: K-splitting across both harts of a minion for large K, grouped K-split (batches 4 rows per semaphore exchange), tiled K for very large K, x2-row batching (reuses activation loads across 2 output rows when row-stride alignment permits), and an N-split path specifically for small-M shapes (keeps many harts busy when M is small by splitting the OUTPUT COLUMN dimension across harts instead of rows).
hackathon_llama32_1b_REHAN_PERMISSION_an.confirmed_his_actual_score_reflects_this: git compare of his authored Q8_0-kernel commit (84405bb7) against his ACTUAL SCORED leaderboard commit (334ec451b8878ca1d883229b54e4d27b51fcb82a, the one that got 14.7096) shows 'diverged' (ahead_by 133, behind_by 1727) -- not a direct ancestor -- BUT fetching mul_mat_Q8_0.c's actual file content at his scored commit shows the SAME sophisticated K-split/N-split/row-vector-accumulate/hardware-scale-convert/x2-row-batch structure (413 lines vs 467 at the other commit, same techniques, presumably a slightly earlier/parallel-evolved snapshot). CONFIRMED: his 14.7096 score already reflects this whole Q8_0 kernel family, not only his separately-analyzed F32 attention tensor-engine work (mul_mat_f32_matrix_engine.c, PR#161).
hackathon_llama32_1b_REHAN_PERMISSION_an.one_still_untried_refinement_identified: His per-block scale handling does ONE fbcx.ps+fcvt.ps.f16 hardware convert PER BLOCK inside q8_dot_tile's loop -- our scale-unpack lever's batched approach (pack 8 block deltas into a contiguous scratch buffer, convert all 8 in ONE fgh.ps+fcvt.ps.f16 call) does roughly 8x fewer scale-conversion instructions for the same row. This is a genuine, not-yet-tried micro-refinement layerable on top of his already-proven-strong kernel -- worth attempting AFTER first verifying his base kernel works correctly through our own oracle, not before.
hackathon_llama32_1b_REHAN_PERMISSION_an.revised_plan: Adopt RehanQasim's proven Q8_0 kernel (with explicit attribution in every commit message noting authorization) as the PR#170 base -- this alone should get llama32_1b close to or matching his 14.7096, a far larger jump than anything independently built this session (which topped out around +0.39-0.84%). hackathon_llama32_1b_ABI_COMPAT_and_THRE._doc: MAJOR CORRECTION + EXECUTION, 2026-07-23. Ryan explicitly rejected the prior 'adopt Rehan's kernel wholesale' plan as premature: Rehan personally told Ryan he (Rehan) has NOT found all the proper optimizations, he is 'doing just enough to win.' This entry documents the full verified lever inventory, the real ABI/primitive-availability findings discovered while trying to actually adopt his kernel, and the resulting 3-PR empirical comparison actually built, oracle-verified, and pushed.

full_lever_inventory_table.mask_hoist: Everyone has it (us/Rehan/ChiruGuru99) -- baseline, not a differentiator.
full_lever_inventory_table.row_vector_accumulate: Rehan + ChiruGuru99 have it, we didn't build it standalone. ChiruGuru99's own profiling said this class of change 'changed nothing' -- likely small.
full_lever_inventory_table.hardware_scale_convert_per_block: Rehan has it (fbcx.ps+fcvt.ps.f16 once per block inside q8_dot_tile).
full_lever_inventory_table.hardware_scale_convert_batched_8: WE have it (this session's own standalone lever, oracle-verified separately) -- packs 8 blocks' deltas, one fgh.ps+fcvt.ps.f16 for all 8. Rehan does NOT have this -- his is per-block, ours does ~8x fewer scale-convert instructions per group.
full_lever_inventory_table.cache_line_owned_atomic_free_stores: WE tried, PROVEN CATASTROPHICALLY BROKEN (16x parallelism collapse, real board data). ChiruGuru99 tried and disabled it too ('unsafe', never diagnosed why -- consistent with the same structural flaw). Rehan doesn't use this approach at all. Dead end as naively built by two independent parties.
full_lever_inventory_table.weight_row_prefetch_8x_per_row: WE tried, PROVEN REGRESSION (-3.3%, real board data, tight CV both sides). Dead end as originally built (reused an 8-way cooperative-worker partition helper that didn't match this loop's single-owner access pattern).
full_lever_inventory_table.weight_row_prefetch_light_1x_per_row: WE built + oracle-verified a from-scratch reimplementation (one CSR-write loop per row, not 8). Rehan's kernel has NO prefetch at all. Genuinely untapped by him.
full_lever_inventory_table.k_splitting: Rehan has it (both harts of a minion split K, exchange via L2SCP + semaphore). CRITICAL FINDING: depends on et_sem_post/et_sem_wait/et_shire_l2scp_local -- NONE of these exist anywhere in current shared main's platform.h (grepped full et-kernels/src tree at f67c2b2a30a24bf9354857cde0f233620a20eb23, confirmed absent). His fork added this semaphore infra itself; it never landed on the shared tip. Cannot safely port without a real reference to verify a hand-written semaphore/barrier against -- exactly the kind of blind guess that produced the cache-line-stores regression. Checked llama32_1b's actual shapes: K_blocks<=256 (TILE_KB) for every one of its Q8_0 matmuls, so K-split's own 'small rows' carve-out (rows_per_minion<=2, K_blocks>=64) is the ONLY branch that would ever fire for this model, specifically helping k_proj/v_proj (M=512, GQA num_kv_heads=8*head_dim=64) where plain per-hart striping only engages 512 of 2048 harts (25% utilization) -- a REAL, still-open gap, left flagged rather than silently dropped or blindly implemented.
full_lever_inventory_table.x2_row_batching: Rehan has it (q8_dot_compute_x2_aligned, gated on nb01%32==0). Verified this condition IS satisfied for llama32_1b's actual row strides (nb01 = K_blocks*34 bytes; for K=2048, K_blocks=64, nb01=2176, 2176%32==0). Real, applicable technique.
full_lever_inventory_table.n_split_small_M: Rehan has it but applicability to llama32_1b's actual decode calling convention was never conclusively resolved this session -- flagged uncertain, not used in any combo.
full_lever_inventory_table.uberkernel_op_fusion: Nobody (not us, not Rehan, not ChiruGuru99) has this enabled for any model in this track. Real infra exists in a separate lineage of aifoundry-org/llama.cpp, off by default. Untouched opportunity, not attempted this session due to time/risk.
full_lever_inventory_table.tensor_engine_q8_0_gemv: Nobody has this for the N=1 decode case, including Rehan (his F32 tensor-engine work targets attention, not Q8_0 weight projections, and explicitly doesn't cover the small-N GEMV case). Highest ceiling, highest risk, untried.

hackathon_llama32_1b_ABI_COMPAT_and_THRE.critical_abi_finding_params_struct: Attempting to actually adopt Rehan's kernel revealed his entry_point uses `struct ggml_et_mm_q8_params` (with a trailing `bias` field) while our own prior kernel used the older `struct ggml_et_binary_params` (first 3 fields identical, no bias) -- these are ABI-COMPATIBLE by struct-prefix layout, which is WHY our old kernel worked despite using the 'wrong' type. Checked ggml-et-ops.cpp's actual dispatcher at the current pinned commit (f67c2b2a...): it ALREADY constructs and passes `ggml_et_mm_q8_params` to mul_mat_Q8_0 (line 384-388), meaning Rehan's kernel is the more CORRECTLY-typed match for the current dispatch contract, not a foreign ABI. No host-side changes needed to adopt his signature.
hackathon_llama32_1b_ABI_COMPAT_and_THRE.critical_missing_primitives_finding: Grepped current main's platform.h (et-kernels/src) for every primitive Rehan's K-split code calls: et_shire_l2scp_local, ET_BARRIER_MINION, flush_to_l2, WAIT_CACHEOPS, FENCE, atomic_store_f32, get_hart_id are ALL present -- but et_sem_post, et_sem_wait, and a whole-tensor evict_region_past_l2 helper are ABSENT from the entire et-kernels/src tree (only a per-batch evict_to_l2(addr,nlines,stride) exists, not a whole-region wrapper). Confirmed via direct fetch+grep of ggml_tensor.h, tensor.h, math_fp.h, quants.h too -- genuinely absent, not just misnamed.

three_combo_execution.methodology: Rather than guess which lever combination wins, built and oracle-verified THREE genuinely different, non-overlapping compositions, staged on the three existing reusable PRs (per the standing 'reuse PRs, don't spam the board' rule), and let real board data decide -- exactly Ryan's explicit strategy ('pr all different options and see what works').
three_combo_execution.combo_A_pr168: Rehan's Q8_0 GEMM structure (mask-hoist + row-vector-accumulate + per-block hardware scale-convert + x2-row-batching), freshly rebuilt from source against current main, with the K-split/K-split-group branches REMOVED (unavailable primitives, see above) -- since llama32_1b's shapes never exceed TILE_KB anyway, this is a clean, honest 'his structure, minus the part we can't safely verify.' Commit DarthCeltic/llama.cpp@daf3f91723db2d6b76d068fc891fac277577a217 (branch llama32_1b-combo-a-rehan-base). Attributed to RehanQasim-dev in the commit message with Ryan's reported authorization.
three_combo_execution.combo_B_pr169: Combo A + our own light single-call-per-row prefetch (a lever Rehan's kernel does not have at all -- genuinely additive, not redundant). Commit DarthCeltic/llama.cpp@3d573fc6c046b23c6d61a35fc4e4c30dc33837e8 (branch llama32_1b-combo-b-rehan-plus-prefetch).
three_combo_execution.combo_C_pr170: A DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT combination, not a superset: mask-hoist + light-prefetch + our OWN batched-8 scale-convert, trading away x2-row-batching and row-vector-accumulate deferral. Investigated porting batched-8 scale-convert into Rehan's deferred-accumulation design and found it needs an arbitrary-lane (0..7) vector-to-scalar extract that has no verified ISA support in this codebase (only a FIXED lane-4 extract pattern, fmvz.x.ps, is ever used, always after a pairwise reduction) -- inventing one blind was judged the same category of risk that caused the cache-line-stores regression, so declined. Commit DarthCeltic/llama.cpp@a89691c59f53101a45476d6818d2cff2c75c4f61 (branch llama32_1b-combo-c-batched-scaleconvert). This composition lets real board data show whether x2-row B-load reuse or batched scale-convert is worth more for this model's shapes -- genuine non-overlapping bet, not just a bigger pile of levers.
three_combo_execution.verification: All three combos oracle-verified via llama.cpp's own test-backend-ops against the real ET software-emulator backend: every MUL_MAT(type_a=q8_0, type_b=f32, m=16, n=1..9, k=256) case OK, 9/9, for all three, before any push to the shared board.

hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_A_REAL_RESULT.result: llama32_1b: candidate 13.7142 tok/s vs fresh baseline (current main) 13.4548 vs leaderboard best 14.7096. hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_A_REAL_RESULT.other_model_results_this_run: Several other regression models (gemma3n_e2b, tinyllama11b, smollm2_135m/360m/17b, rwkv7_15b, qwen25_05b) also scored below their own historical baseline in this same run -- worth investigating whether removing K-split has a genuine cross-model cost (many small LLMs are also Q8_0-quantized and may hit the same K-split-eligible shapes we skipped). qwen3_8b/deepseek_r1_15b/smolvlm_256m crashed with the SAME 'Device or resource busy' infra error partway through this same run (board contention from other concurrent CI activity) -- infra noise, not our code; the llama32_1b and early-model results in this same run are trustworthy because they completed before the board got contended.
hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_A_REAL_RESULT.next: Awaiting Combo B (PR#169, + light prefetch) and Combo C (PR#170, batched-8 scale-convert instead of x2-row-batch) real results, retriggered one-at-a-time (empty commits) after board-contention was diagnosed from the first simultaneous push.

hackathon_llama32_1b_PREFETCH_REAL_HW_CR._doc: Real (non-infra) board crash found + diagnosed + fixed. Combo B v1 (PR#169, DarthCeltic/llama.cpp@3d573fc6c046b23c6d61a35fc4e4c30dc33837e8) passed the small test-backend-ops oracle fixture (9/9 OK, m=16 n=1..9 k=256) but CRASHED on the real full model on real hardware.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PREFETCH_REAL_HW_CR.crash_signature: 'ET: stream error detected at synchronization point. Code: 0,Type: 6' repeated on every dispatch during llama-server's warmup empty-run, ending in 'llama-bench exited rc=-6' (SIGABRT). Combo A (identical kernel minus the prefetch addition) ran the SAME real model cleanly (13.7142 tok/s, zero stream errors) in the same session -- isolating the cause to the prefetch lever specifically, not the underlying Rehan structure.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PREFETCH_REAL_HW_CR.root_cause: prefetch_row_light() issued the prefetch_va CSR (0x81f) in a loop but never drained/waited for it. Every OTHER cache-management CSR operation anywhere in this codebase (flush_to_l2, evict_to_l2) is always paired with FENCE+WAIT_CACHEOPS by its caller -- prefetch_row_light was the only cache-op-CSR-issuing function in either combo that skipped this. The small oracle fixture is a single isolated MUL_MAT dispatch; it never queues enough back-to-back kernel launches for an undrained prefetch backlog to overflow/corrupt stream state. A real 16-layer decode loop dispatches thousands of times per token, giving the bug room to surface. THIS IS WHY THE ORACLE FIXTURE ALONE IS NOT SUFFICIENT for hardware-timing/queue-depth-dependent bugs -- test-backend-ops verifies numerical correctness of a single call, not concurrency/drain correctness across many.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PREFETCH_REAL_HW_CR.fix: Added FENCE + WAIT_CACHEOPS immediately after the prefetch_row_light() CSR-issue loop, matching the established drain pattern. Combo B v2 (DarthCeltic/llama.cpp@a772c806b24900fa491ec92bad0a496b5230434c) re-verified against the same small fixture (still 9/9 OK, as expected -- that fixture can't prove the fix either, only a real board run can). Pushed to PR#169, real-hardware confirmation pending.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PREFETCH_REAL_HW_CR.risk_management_decision: Combo C v1 also included the same unfixed prefetch call. Rather than ship the same unconfirmed bug into a second PR, rebuilt Combo C v2 WITHOUT prefetch at all (mask-hoist + batched-8 scale-convert only, isolating that lever alone against the Combo A base already proven clean on real hardware). This keeps prefetch as a single-variable test confined to PR#169, so a second real-hardware run will cleanly tell us whether the drain fix actually works, without confounding it with another new lever.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PREFETCH_REAL_HW_CR.general_lesson: For ANY future ET-SoC1 kernel lever that issues a cache-management or prefetch CSR, always pair it with FENCE+WAIT_CACHEOPS (or the equivalent drain) even if the small test-backend-ops fixture passes without it -- passing that fixture is necessary but NOT sufficient proof of correctness for hardware-queue/ordering-sensitive code. A real full-model board run is the only oracle that can catch this class of bug.

hackathon_llama32_1b_THREE_COMBO_FINAL_R._doc: CANONICAL final results for the 3-combo empirical comparison. Supersedes/completes hackathon_llama32_1b_ABI_COMPAT_and_THREE_COMBO_PLAN_20260723, hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_A_REAL_RESULT_20260723, and hackathon_llama32_1b_PREFETCH_REAL_HW_CRASH_and_FIX_20260723.

combo_A_rehan_structure_only.content: Rehan's Q8_0 GEMM structure (mask-hoist + row-vector-accumulate + per-block hardware scale-convert + x2-row-batching), K-split excluded (missing semaphore primitives on current main).
combo_A_rehan_structure_only.real_result: llama32_1b: 13.7142 tok/s vs fresh baseline 13.4548 vs leaderboard best 14.7096. Beat baseline +1.93% (passes 1% min bar). Below leaderboard-best by -6.8% (gate fail, correctly -- competition mode requires beating leaderboard best).
combo_A_rehan_structure_only.verdict: BEST of the three real results. Real, clean, zero crashes. Currently live on all three PRs (#168/#169/#170) as of end of session.

combo_B_plus_light_prefetch.content: Combo A + single-call-per-row DRAM prefetch (prefetch_va CSR 0x81f), a lever Rehan's kernel does not have at all.
combo_B_plus_light_prefetch.real_result: CRASHED on real hardware: 'ET: stream error detected at synchronization point... llama-bench exited rc=-6' (SIGABRT) during warmup, on every dispatch. Passed the small test-backend-ops oracle fixture (9/9 OK) but broke on the real full model.
combo_B_plus_light_prefetch.fix_attempted: Added FENCE+WAIT_CACHEOPS drain after the prefetch CSR loop (matching the pattern used for every other cache-op CSR in this codebase). Re-tested on real hardware: IDENTICAL crash recurred. The missing-drain hypothesis was wrong or insufficient.
combo_B_plus_light_prefetch.verdict: ABANDONED. Two real-hardware attempts, both crashed. No further guessing without live device debug access -- reverted PR#169 back to Combo A. This lever is NOT currently viable for this track without deeper access to ET-SoC1 runtime internals than this session has.

combo_C_batched_scale_convert_no_x2.content: Mask-hoist + this session's own batched-8 fp16 scale-convert (packs 8 blocks' deltas, one fgh.ps+fcvt.ps.f16 for all 8), trading away Rehan's x2-row-batching (which needs the deferred-accumulation structure batched-8 doesn't compose safely with, see prior entry for the arbitrary-lane-extract reasoning).
combo_C_batched_scale_convert_no_x2.real_result: llama32_1b: 13.4726 tok/s vs fresh baseline 13.4832 -- essentially FLAT, did not beat baseline (needs >13.6180). WORSE than Combo A (13.7142).
combo_C_batched_scale_convert_no_x2.verdict: Real, valuable NEGATIVE finding: x2-row-batching's B-load-reuse benefit is worth MORE than batching the scale-convert instructions. The trade was net negative. Reverted PR#170 back to Combo A.

hackathon_llama32_1b_THREE_COMBO_FINAL_R.headline_conclusion: Of every lever combination actually built and verified on real hardware this session: Combo A (Rehan's proven structure, minus the K-split branches we couldn't safely verify) is the strongest real, working result at 13.7142 tok/s -- a genuine +1.9% improvement over stock main, but still -6.8% short of RehanQasim-dev's leaderboard-best 14.7096. Both attempted differentiators (light-prefetch, batched-scale-convert-instead-of-x2) made things WORSE or crashed outright. hackathon_llama32_1b_KSPLIT_SCOPE_CORREC.ksplit_scope_correction: Combo D's commit message said the small-rows K-split carve-out 'specifically helps k_proj/v_proj at M=512.' Re-checked the actual condition (rows_per_minion<=2, i.e. M<=2048) against ALL of llama32_1b's real Q8_0 matmul shapes (confirmed exact via HF config: hidden=2048, intermediate=8192, num_attention_heads=32, num_key_value_heads=8, head_dim=64, num_hidden_layers=16, vocab=128256): q_proj (M=2048), o_proj (M=2048), down_proj (M=2048, K=8192), k_proj/v_proj (M=512) ALL satisfy rows_per_minion<=2 and so ALL route through Combo D's small-rows branch -- not just k/v-proj. For q/o/down-proj, M already equals STRIDE_M(2048) exactly, so plain per-hart striping already gives 100% hart utilization there; K-split's benefit for THOSE three is a LATENCY win (2 harts split one row's K range, finishing it faster), not a utilization win. Only k/v-proj (M=512, 25% utilization under plain striping) gets the utilization win. gate_proj/up_proj (M=8192, K=2048) and lm_head (M=128256, K=2048) do NOT qualify for K-split at all (rows_per_minion=8 and ~126, both >2) and correctly stay on Combo A's proven simple-path/x2-batching route. Net: Combo D's real scope is broader than documented -- it touches 5 of the 7 distinct Q8_0 matmul shapes in the model, not 2. This raises the plausible ceiling of Combo D's real improvement if it proves correct on hardware, since it isn't limited to just the smallest, least-frequent matmuls.

hackathon_llama32_1b_PUSH_MARCHING_ORDER._doc: Standing operational rule for all future pushes to aifoundry-org/hf-hackathon PRs #168/#169/#170 (or their successors), established 2026-07-24 after directly confirming the workflow's concurrency mechanics.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PUSH_MARCHING_ORDER.confirmed_mechanism: aifoundry-org/hf-hackathon/.github/workflows/trusted-llama32-pr.yml declares `concurrency: group: trusted-llama32-pr-<PR#>, cancel-in-progress: true`. Directly verified: pushing a new commit to a PR branch correctly auto-cancels any prior queued/in-progress run in that same PR's concurrency group (confirmed via GitHub API -- the earlier stuck run's status flipped to conclusion=cancelled the moment a newer commit was pushed to the same PR).
hackathon_llama32_1b_PUSH_MARCHING_ORDER.rule: Do NOT hold back on pushing a new/updated candidate to a PR out of fear of orphaned locks, piled-up queued runs, or leaving a stuck run dangling -- the concurrency group handles that automatically and correctly, per-PR-number. Each PR (168/169/170) is its own independent concurrency group; pushes to different PRs never block each other. A stuck 'queued, no runner assigned' run is NOT evidence of a lock problem needing manual cleanup -- it resolves itself (via cancellation) the instant a newer push lands, and if it stays queued after that, the cause is the self-hosted runner not picking up jobs, not a stale concurrency lock.
hackathon_llama32_1b_PUSH_MARCHING_ORDER.practical_implication: Push freely and immediately when a new combo is ready to test -- do not wait, do not add artificial delays between pushes to 'avoid contention' (that was based on an earlier, since-corrected theory about the board legitimately being busy from concurrent traffic). If a run sits queued indefinitely, that is signal about runner/board availability, not about our own push cadence, and the fix is either waiting for the runner to come back or pushing again anyway (harmless) to get a fresh queued attempt ready to be picked up the moment it does.

combo_G_tensor_engine_decode.what: HIGHEST CEILING, HIGHEST UNCERTAINTY lever this session. Changes host-side dispatch in ggml-et-ops.cpp (not kernel code): the Q8_0xF32 MUL_MAT tensor-engine path (mul_mat_Q8_0_matrix_engine.c) previously only dispatched for N>=47, always falling through to the scalar kernel for anything smaller -- including decode's N=1, which NOBODY (not Rehan, not this session before now) has tried routing through the tensor engine. Investigated the tensor-engine kernel source directly: it already has real n_cur<TILE_N edge-case handling down to a single row (bias-preload path checks n_cur>0..>4 individually) -- the >=47 floor is a dispatch heuristic, not a kernel requirement. Lowered the floor to N>=1, oracle-confirmed numerically correct at m=16,k=256,n=1..9 (previously always scalar-dispatched, now tensor-engine-dispatched, same correct answers).
combo_G_tensor_engine_decode.open_question: Whether tensor-engine dispatch is actually FASTER than the scalar kernel for a single N=1 GEMV is genuinely unknown -- its setup/dequant-cache-priming cost is normally amortized over many N-tiles in prefill, not one. Sys-emu is explicitly not a performance oracle per the hackathon's own martin.md guide. Only real board data can answer this. This is a shared dispatch change affecting all 11 regression models' Q8_0 MUL_MAT calls, not just llama32_1b -- the existing all-or-nothing gate is the correct test for whether it's safe everywhere.
combo_G_tensor_engine_decode.oracle_status: 9/9 OK on standard m=16 k=256 n=1..9 sweep, now routing through the tensor engine instead of the scalar kernel for every one of those cases.

Traced the exact race by hand, then confirmed the fix pattern against the already-shipped reference kernel.
hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F_DEADLOCK_CO.exact_mechanism: Combo F's use_ksplit branch resets ready_ctr/consumed_ctr to 0 and re-barriers INSIDE the n-loop, i.e. once per N-tile within a single kernel dispatch, not once per dispatch. Hart1 (producer)'s transition from iteration n to n+1 is: scp_signal(ready, wid_final) [last row of n] -> scp_signal(ready, 0) [reset for n+1] -> scp_signal(consumed, 0) -> et_barrier() -- with NOTHING between the first and second steps to force hart1 to wait for hart0 to actually consume n's last row first. If hart1 reaches the reset before hart0's scp_wait(ready_ctr, wid_final) for n's last row observes the real value, ready_ctr is overwritten to 0 out from under that wait -- a value hart0 is waiting for that will never reappear. Hart1 then blocks at ITS OWN et_barrier() for n+1, which hart0 can never reach because it is still stuck earlier in the code waiting on n's stale ready value. Both harts deadlock, permanently, each waiting on the other -- not slow, not eventually-consistent, genuinely forever until an external timeout (240 minutes) kills the job.
hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F_DEADLOCK_CO.why_untested: This can only fire when N>1 within a single kernel dispatch -- decode's N=1 gives hart1 no 'next iteration' to race into within the same call. Every oracle test this session used n=1 (chosen for sysemu speed), so this was structurally invisible to all of it, including the purpose-built grouped-tier and small-rows-tier shape tests. The trusted gate's PP256 benchmark (prompt processing, N=256 in one dispatch) is exactly the scenario that guarantees this fires -- which is almost certainly why the real run hung instead of ever reaching a llama32_1b decode-only result.
hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F_DEADLOCK_CO.confirmed_fix_pattern: Compared against the ALREADY-SHIPPED, presumably battle-tested mul_mat_Q8_0_matrix_engine.c (the tensor-engine kernel Combo G dispatches to): it resets ready_ctr/consumed_ctr exactly ONCE, OUTSIDE the entire batch/N-tile loop nest, then lets wid climb monotonically across every unit of work in the whole dispatch -- it never re-enters a reset mid-dispatch. This is the correct, safe pattern. Combo F's per-n reset-and-rebarrier was a deviation from this reference that introduced the race. Any future K-split attempt must reset once before the i3/i2/n loop nest begins and use a single monotonically-increasing wid for the entire dispatch, exactly mirroring the reference kernel's structure -- not re-derive the handshake independently.
hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F_DEADLOCK_CO.queued_candidates_checked_clean: Combo G (tensor-engine dispatch, PR#168): does not touch this synchronization code at all -- dispatches to the reference kernel described above, which already has the correct pattern. Verified safe from this specific bug class. Combo B v3 (prefetch fix, PR#170): prefetch_row_light has no persistent cross-call handshake state (stateless CSR issue + local drain per call) -- nothing to race against regardless of N. Verified safe.
hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F_DEADLOCK_CO.lesson: The x31-stride bug (Combo B) and this deadlock (Combo F) share the same root lesson: when reusing a synchronization/CSR primitive, diff the new usage against every EXISTING, already-proven usage of that exact primitive in this codebase line-by-line before trusting it -- don't re-derive the calling convention from first principles or partial recall. Both bugs were found only when this discipline was actually followed (for B, after being pushed to compare byte-for-byte; for F, after being pushed to do a real trace instead of accepting 'oracle passed' as sufficient).

hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_G_CATASTROPHI.conclusion: The tensor engine's per-dispatch setup/dequant-cache-priming cost -- designed to amortize over many N-tiles during prefill (its REUSE_MAX/n_groups logic explicitly groups multiple N-tiles to spread that cost) -- completely dominates when there is only ONE N-tile to amortize it over, as in single-token decode. This is not a close call or a noise-level effect; it is a severe, decisive, uniform loss across every model tested. CLOSED: tensor-engine dispatch for N=1 GEMV is NOT viable via this simple threshold-lowering approach. A genuinely different kernel design tuned specifically for N=1 (skipping the reuse/windowing machinery entirely) might still be viable in principle, but the naive 'just lower the dispatch floor' approach is definitively ruled out by real hardware data.

hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F2_REAL_WIN_a.why_this_is_plausible_not_just_infra_noi: The deadlock fix addressed ONE specific mechanism (the per-n reset race) structurally for BOTH the small-rows/primary tier and the grouped tier. If gemma3n_e2b/smollm2_360m/qwen25_05b/rwkv7_15b have shapes landing in the primary or grouped K-split tiers with some untested edge case (e.g. a different rows_per_minion count, a remainder in the 4-row grouping when M isn't a clean multiple of 4*STRIDE_M_KSPLIT, or a different K_blocks value near a boundary condition), there could be a SEPARATE bug in those tiers that this session's narrow oracle coverage never exercised.
hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F2_REAL_WIN_a.next_step_before_trusting_this_as_a_clea: Check each of the 4 crashing models' actual Q8_0 matmul shapes (hidden_size, intermediate_size, num_kv_heads, etc. from their HF configs, same diligence already applied to llama32_1b) against use_ksplit/use_ksplit_group's trigger conditions, to determine whether they are landing in a genuinely untested K-split code path. hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F2_CRASH_ROOT.conclusion: The crash is very likely a genuine real-hardware-only timing/race issue in the L2SCP producer/consumer handshake -- same bug CLASS as the original prefetch SIGABRT (also real-hw-only, never reproduced in sysemu, also rc=-6) and the original K-split deadlock (also real-hw-only, sysemu couldn't reproduce it either). Traced the post-fix handshake by hand (hart1: wait-on-consumed(prev) -> write -> signal-ready(new); hart0: wait-on-ready(new) -> read -> signal-consumed(new)) and it is a correctly-ordered single-buffered blocking handshake with proper back-pressure -- no logic race is visible in the source. Leading hypothesis: an ET-runtime stream-watchdog/heartbeat (the same 'ET: stream error detected at synchronization point' class of message seen in the original prefetch bug) may fire on timing/contention grounds specific to running many back-to-back K-split dispatches across many layers (these 4 models have 24-32 layers vs llama32_1b's 16) and/or L2SCP contention from concurrent model runs during the same benchmark sweep -- not confirmed, would need real board time with per-model isolation to pin down further.
hackathon_llama32_1b_COMBO_F2_CRASH_ROOT.why_this_matters_for_the_gate: Independent of whether the root cause gets fixed: a crash in ANY tracked regression model is an automatic gate fail regardless of how good llama32_1b's own result is (the gate requires all OTHER tracked models to stay within 1% of their own historical best -- a SIGABRT crash is not 'within tolerance', it's a hard failure). So Combo F v2's genuine +2.60% llama32_1b win was never shippable as-is. This is a harder constraint than a simple regression tradeoff.

hackathon_llama32_1b_CRITICAL_REAL_GATE_.finding_1_real_llama32_1b_bar: The competition-mode gate for llama32_1b does NOT just require beating your own paired baseline by 1%. hackathon_llama32_1b_CRITICAL_REAL_GATE_.finding_2_regression_bar_is_a_ratchet: The OTHER 11 regression models are NOT compared against a fixed/stable reference -- 'reference_tokens_per_second' is a running historical-best RATCHET that only ever goes up, updated whenever ANY candidate run (regardless of what it targets) scores higher for that model. Direct evidence: gemma3n_e2b's bar was 1.4962/1.5734 on the ORIGINAL Combo A establishing run (run 30050594100, hours ago) and PASSED at 1.5764/1.5738. The SAME kernel code (Combo A, unmodified) re-run tonight scored 1.7919 and 1.8048 -- HIGHER than the original passing score -- but FAILED because the bar itself had ratcheted up to 2.1110 sometime during the session (most likely from one of our own earlier candidate pushes hitting a lucky high sample on gemma3n_e2b as a side effect of sharing the same Q8_0 kernel). More pushes on the same code have pure downside risk and no upside once llama32_1b's own bar (finding 1) is already unreachable.
hackathon_llama32_1b_CRITICAL_REAL_GATE_.finding_3_genuine_board_infrastructure_i: PR170's Combo A revert run (e6ee24ce, run 30064126304, 03:23 UTC) shows SIX regression models (smollm2_17b, rwkv7_15b, qwen25_05b, qwen3_8b, deepseek_r1_15b, smolvlm_256m) all failing identically with 'llama-server exited before model loaded' plus a garbled scratchpad-address-format dump -- a cascading board/runtime-level failure, on completely unmodified, safe Combo A code. hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_KERNEL_AUDI.result: Negative, definitively. Grepped all sibling kernel files (rms_norm_f32.c, rms_norm_mul_f32.c, rope_f32.c, softmax_f32.c, glu_f32.c, unary_f32.c, norm_f32.c) for any literal CSR-write instruction ('csrw') -- zero hits in every file. mul_mat_Q8_0.c is the ONLY kernel in the entire et-kernels/src tree that issues explicit CSR writes at all (for K-split's L2SCP signaling and the (reverted) prefetch_va CSR). The sibling kernels use only simple paired-float RVV-style SIMD instructions (flw.ps/fmadd.ps/fswizz.ps etc) with no custom CSR/mask setup whatsoever -- there is no equivalent 'redundant setup reissued every call' pattern to hoist, because there's no setup instruction there in the first place. Read rms_norm_f32.c in full as the representative case: its only per-iteration redundancy is a cheap scalar broadcast (fbc.ps of the precomputed scale) inside the write loop, not a heavyweight CSR call -- not worth a dedicated fix.
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_KERNEL_AUDI.conclusion: The mask-hoist technique (and the whole class of 'find a redundant CSR setup and hoist it out of the loop' optimization) is specific to mul_mat_Q8_0's dequantization/scale-handling machinery, not a generalizable pattern across this kernel suite. This lead is CLOSED -- do not re-audit these files again for this pattern.

hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE._doc: CORRECTS hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_KERNEL_AUDIT_CLOSED_20260724, which was WRONG -- it grepped only for literal 'csrw' and concluded no sibling kernel had mask-hoist-style overhead. The real mask-hoist mechanism uses 'mova.x.m'/'mov.m.x' (vector-mask save/set/restore), not 'csrw' at all. Re-audited every kernel in et-kernels/src with the correct grep. This is the complete, honest, labeled inventory the user asked for after pushing back on giving up too early.
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.authoritative_op_list: Read directly from ggml_backend_et_graph_compute's switch statement (ggml-et.cpp) -- the actual, complete op set this backend handles: MUL, ADD, SUB (all -> el_map_f32), MUL_MAT (-> mul_mat_Q8_0 or mul_mat_f32 or matrix-engine variants), MUL_MAT_ID (MoE, unused by llama32_1b), ROPE, RMS_NORM (+fused RMS_NORM_MUL), NORM, UNARY, IM2COL (conv, unused), SCALE, GLU, SOFT_MAX, GET_ROWS, CONT, SET_ROWS, plus no-op metadata ops (RESHAPE/VIEW/PERMUTE/TRANSPOSE).
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.decode_path_kernel_inventory_llama32_1b: Per decode token, per layer: RMS_NORM_MUL x2 (input norm + post-attn norm), MUL_MAT Q8_0 x7 (q/k/v/o/gate/up/down -- already fully audited this session), ROPE x2 (Q,K), MUL_MAT F32 x2 (QKt and attn x V), SOFT_MAX x1, GLU x1 (SwiGLU), ADD x2 (residuals, via el_map_f32), SET_ROWS x2 (K and V cache write). Plus once per token overall: GET_ROWS (embedding lookup), final RMS_NORM_MUL, MUL_MAT Q8_0 (lm_head). CONT/mul_mat_f32_matrix_engine exist in the backend but were not confirmed to fire on llama32_1b's specific decode graph (matrix-engine attention has its own dispatch threshold; CONT may only fire for certain KV-cache layouts).
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.clean_kernels_no_mask_overhead: rms_norm_f32.c (read in full, zero mask instructions, uses fbc.ps directly), rms_norm_mul_f32.c (same, zero mask instructions), mul_mat_f32.c (F32 attention matmul, zero mask instructions), mul_mat_f32_matrix_engine.c (zero mask instructions), cont_f32.c, cont_f16.c (zero mask instructions). These are genuinely not targets for the mask-hoist pattern -- confirmed, not assumed.
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.already_well_hoisted_kernels: el_map_f32.c (residual ADD/MUL/SUB): mask save/set/restore happens once per block-function CALL, and that call already happens once per row (not per element) -- for decode specifically total_rows=1 (single-token hidden state), so there is no further row-level redundancy to hoist for the DECODE metric specifically (would matter more for prefill's 256 rows). scale_f32.c, unary_f32.c: same pattern, hoisted once per invocation already.
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.NEW_FINDING_rope_high_confidence: rope_f32.c: the mask save/set(0xFF)/restore sequence (lines ~461-483 in the is_neox branch) happens ONCE PER WORK-UNIT inside the 'for (wu = start_wu; wu < end_wu; ++wu)' loop, where wu enumerates (head, seq_pos, batch) combinations -- NOT hoisted outside that loop. The mask value is always the same constant (0xFF, all lanes) regardless of wu, exactly the structural signature that made mask-hoist a proven win in mul_mat_Q8_0. For llama32_1b decode (seq_len=1, batch=1): Q-rope has 32 work-units (num_attention_heads), K-rope has 8 (num_key_value_heads) -- 40 work-units/layer x 16 layers = 640 redundant mask save/set/restore triples per decode token. HIGH CONFIDENCE real, structurally simple to fix (hoist the 3 asm lines outside the wu loop, matching exactly how mask-hoist fixed mul_mat_Q8_0), and easy to oracle-verify (pure refactor, no algorithmic change, output must be bit-identical).
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.NEW_FINDING_glu_swiglu_high_confidence: glu_f32.c's block_swiglu (and block_geglu) do mask save/set/restore ONCE PER CACHE-LINE call, and the outer entry_point calls block_swiglu once per 16-element cache-line chunk (elements_per_cacheline=16, hardcoded) via 'for (cl = start_cacheline; cl < end_cacheline; cl++)' -- NOT hoisted across cache lines within a thread's work assignment. For llama32_1b's intermediate_size=8192 (gate/up proj width), a single layer's SwiGLU spans 8192/16=512 cache-lines total (divided across active threads, but each thread still redoes the mask cycle for every cache-line it owns) x16 layers. Real, same structural signature as RoPE, likely comparable or larger total redundant-cycle count depending on actual thread count used for this op.
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.PENDING_FINDING_softmax_needs_deeper_tra: softmax_f32.c (562 lines, most complex kernel in the suite) has mask save/set/restore at MANY distinct sites across a two-pass (pass1_range/pass2_range) online-softmax structure, some clearly inside nested sub-loops (e.g. a 'for (k=0;k<8;k++)' loop containing its own mask setup at line ~248). Confirmed NOT already fully hoisted, but the exact redundant-cycle count and the safest hoist point were not fully traced this session (needs careful reading given the numerical-stability-critical online-softmax logic -- do not touch without full understanding, more failure-prone to get wrong than RoPE/GLU's simpler structure).
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.SMALLER_FINDING_set_rows_and_get_rows: set_rows_f32.c's F16-destination path (copy_cache_aligned_f16) resets mask once per 32-element cache-line during KV-cache writes -- smaller magnitude than RoPE/GLU (head_dim=64 means ~2 cache-lines per K/V row x kv_heads x 2(K,V) x layers) but real. get_rows_f32.c has similar per-block mask toggling in several helper functions, but GET_ROWS only fires ONCE per decode token (embedding lookup of the single new token) -- real pattern present, negligible total impact, not worth prioritizing.
hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRE.priority_order_if_pursued: 1) RoPE (640 cycles/token, simple 3-line hoist, easy to verify bit-identical). 2) SwiGLU (comparable or larger cycle count, same simple hoist pattern, slightly more code to touch since block_geglu/block_swiglu are both affected). 3) softmax (potentially the largest kernel by line count and complexity, but needs real time investment to trace safely given the online-softmax numerics -- higher risk of introducing a subtle bug). set_rows/get_rows: real but low-value, not worth board time on their own.

This is an explicit, organizer-reviewed REJECTION, not a credit.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_TRACK_STRUCTURALLY_.conclusion: The live Discord leaderboard bot showing karabambus tied at 1 credit for dncnn does not match the actual committed, CI-enforced repo state (which shows only Ashish-Soni08 with 1 credit, and dncnn explicitly rejected). hackathon_MODEL_PORT_TRACK_STRUCTURALLY_.decision: Model-port track is a structural dead end for new participant credit under current rules. Not pursuing further -- redirected effort back to the Fastest Llama 3.2 1B track (the only track where more real progress is currently possible), specifically the newly-found RoPE/SwiGLU mask-hoist opportunities (see hackathon_llama32_1b_SIBLING_AUDIT_CORRECTION_and_COMPLETE_KERNEL_INVENTORY_20260724).

hackathon_MODEL_PORT_PR172_LIVE_and_GIT_._doc: PR#172 (DistilBERT-SST2 port) is live: https://github.com/aifoundry-org/hf-hackathon/pull/172. Also root-caused and fixed a real infra gotcha that will matter for every future push in this session.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_PR172_LIVE_and_GIT_.git_push_hang_root_cause: Every git push attempt in this session's Windows-side Git Bash environment (not WSL2) hung indefinitely, even for a single small commit. Root cause found via GIT_TRACE=1 GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1: git was using Windows' native git-credential-manager (GCM), NOT gh CLI's own stored auth, and GCM's default flow tries an interactive browser/GUI prompt that can never complete in this non-interactive session -- it just hangs forever with zero error output. Fix: `gh auth setup-git` (configures git's credential.helper to shell out to `gh auth git-credential` instead of GCM). After this one-time fix, pushes complete instantly. IMPORTANT for the rest of this session: this fix is a global git config change (persists), so all FUTURE pushes from this Windows Git Bash environment should now be fast -- don't waste time re-diagnosing this if a future push seems slow for a different reason.

hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CL._doc: Real, verified finding while attempting the second model-port conveyor candidate (ModernBERT multilingual sentiment). Important negative result -- do not repeat this mistake with future N-way (N>2) classification candidates.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CL.model_attempted: clapAI/modernBERT-base-multilingual-sentiment (revision baa7f26fee4eca5aec35538caa5fdda7b86d83c6, apache-2.0). 3-way classification (negative/neutral/positive), unlike DistilBERT-SST2's clean binary (2-way) task.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CL.conversion_and_load_succeeded: GGUF conversion via convert_hf_to_gguf.py worked cleanly (138 tensors, 600MB, correctly captured RoPE theta=160000/swa_theta=10000 confirming ModernBERT's alternating local/global attention). Loaded against real ET backend in sysemu with full 23/23 layer offload, clean 608-node graph -- structurally this ported correctly, same as DistilBERT.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CL.the_real_finding: llama.cpp's --rerank / LLAMA_POOLING_TYPE_RANK path returns a single scalar relevance_score regardless of the model's actual n_cls_out. For DistilBERT (n_cls_out=2) this scalar matched the oracle's positive-class logit closely (2.4789 board vs 2.5304 oracle, ~2% diff, correct). For ModernBERT (n_cls_out=3), the real board score (-2.703847646713257, captured after a genuinely slow ~150s+ request -- NOT a networking fluke, verified 3 times) does NOT closely match ANY of the oracle's 3 real class logits (negative=-3.357, neutral=-1.115, positive=+3.285 -- closest is negative at a 0.65 absolute gap, too large to call correct given DistilBERT's own ~0.05 gap was the bar). This means the rerank/RANK-pooling path in this llama.cpp fork does not cleanly or interpretably support N-way (N>2) classification heads -- it is designed for binary relevance scoring, consistent with its name and typical retrieval-reranking use case.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CL.action_taken: Did NOT submit a ModernBERT PR with an unverified/likely-incorrect correctness claim. This is a real architectural limitation of the current --rerank path, not a flaw in the port itself -- a genuine, reportable finding, distinct from a personal mistake.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CL.lesson_for_future_candidates: Before committing full effort to any future classification-model candidate, check the model's config.json num_labels/id2label FIRST -- only pursue genuinely BINARY (2-label) classification models through this exact playbook (--rerank endpoint) until/unless someone verifies how llama.cpp's rank pooling should correctly handle N>2 classes (might need a different endpoint, a code change to expose per-class scores, or is simply out of scope for --rerank entirely).
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CL.pivoting_to: JeremiahZ/roberta-base-sst2 or similar -- genuinely binary (SST-2 task, positive/negative only), RoBERTa architecture (distinct pretraining lineage from DistilBERT/ModernBERT even though all route through the same llama.cpp LLM_ARCH_BERT graph builder), already registered in convert_hf_to_gguf.py (RobertaModel/RobertaForSequenceClassification).
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CL.unrelated_infra_note: Also confirmed real request latency for larger encoder models (23-layer ModernBERT) on sysemu can genuinely exceed 150-200 seconds for a single /rerank request -- this is NOT the WSL2 networking flakiness I initially suspected; DistilBERT's own first attempt also needed a timeout bump from 30s to 120s before succeeding. Always retry with a much longer client timeout (200s+) before concluding a request is stuck, for any future candidate.

hackathon_MODEL_PORT_PR172_FINAL_CORRECT._doc: Final, corrected state of PR#172: https://github.com/aifoundry-org/hf-hackathon/pull/172 -- now contains TWO real, board-verified model ports (distilbert_sst2 + roberta_sst2) plus an important scoring-logic correction found and fixed mid-session.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_PR172_FINAL_CORRECT.the_real_bug_found_and_fixed: llama.cpp's /rerank endpoint always returns embd[0] (tools/server/server-context.cpp send_rerank(): res->score = embd[0];) -- the raw first logit of the classifier head, with ZERO label-aware selection. This is NOT documented anywhere obvious and is easy to misread as 'the positive class score'. Verified empirically across 2 real models: DistilBERT's embd[0] landed on its POSITIVE logit (oracle 2.5304, board 2.4789, diff 0.05); RoBERTa's embd[0] landed on its NEGATIVE logit (oracle -2.2555, board -1.9601, diff 0.295) -- despite BOTH HF configs declaring the identical id2label={0:NEGATIVE,1:POSITIVE} convention. This means which class embd[0] represents is decided by each architecture's own GGUF conversion class (DistilBertModel vs RobertaModel in convert_hf_to_gguf.py), not a fixed rule. Original scoring code (my own, written for the DistilBert PR) WRONGLY inferred a predicted-label from score>0/score<0 -- fixed to do pure numeric-closeness-to-oracle-reference comparison instead, no label inference at all.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_PR172_FINAL_CORRECT.modernbert_3class_separately_confirmed_u: Also attempted clapAI/modernBERT-base-multilingual-sentiment (3-way: negative/neutral/positive). Real board score (-2.7038) did not closely match ANY of the 3 real oracle logits (negative=-3.357, neutral=-1.115, positive=+3.285 -- closest gap 0.65, too large). Combined with the embd[0]-only mechanism just discovered: /rerank fundamentally cannot expose more than ONE class's raw logit per request, so N-way (N>2) classification models are NOT viable via this exact playbook until/unless a different approach exposes all n_cls_out values. NOT submitted. This is a separate, real, both a documented AND a mechanistically-understood limitation now (see hackathon_MODEL_PORT_RERANK_ENDPOINT_3CLASS_MISMATCH_20260724 for the original finding, now further explained by the embd[0] mechanism).
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_PR172_FINAL_CORRECT.pr172_final_contents: distilbert_sst2 (6-layer DistilBERT, board score 2.4789 vs oracle embd[0]=2.5304, diff 0.05) + roberta_sst2 (12-layer RoBERTa, board score -1.9601 vs oracle embd[0]=-2.2555, diff 0.295) + corrected run_llama_server_benchmark.py (numeric-only scoring, no label inference) + both real oracle scripts + both recipes with full honest writeup of the embd[0] finding.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_PR172_FINAL_CORRECT.lesson_for_any_future_classification_por: Before trusting a /rerank board score as 'verified correct', ALWAYS get the oracle's FULL per-class logits (not just top1/predicted label) and check numeric closeness against logits_all[0] SPECIFICALLY -- never assume index 0 means negative, means positive, or means the predicted class. Each new architecture needs its own board-run to empirically discover which index its own GGUF conversion puts at embd[0].
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_PR172_FINAL_CORRECT.git_push_note: Both distilbert_sst2 and roberta_sst2 ended up as ONE PR (#172) via a single branch (port-distilbert-sst2-v2 on DarthCeltic/hf-hackathon) rather than 2 separate PRs, since roberta's port depended on the same runner-code fix -- avoided a PR-depends-on-PR review complication.
