hackathon_MODEL_PORT_BERT_BASE_CLASSIFIE._doc: Third model-port candidate attempt (textattack/bert-base-uncased-SST-2, plain BertForSequenceClassification, not Distil/Roberta subclass). Real, distinct technical finding -- not submitted.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_BERT_BASE_CLASSIFIE.the_finding: convert_hf_to_gguf.py's base BertModel class (registered for 'BertModel','BertForMaskedLM','CamembertModel','BertForSequenceClassification') converts cleanly (199 tensors, correct shapes reported during conversion) but llama.cpp's C++ loader REJECTS the resulting GGUF at load time: `check_tensor_dims: tensor 'cls.weight' has wrong shape; expected 768, 768, got 768, 2, 1, 1`. The loader hardcodes an expectation that cls.weight is a [n_embd,n_embd]=[768,768] matrix (matching BERT's ORIGINAL pretraining-era NSP pooler shape), not a [n_embd,n_cls_out]=[768,2] downstream classification head. DistilBertModel and RobertaModel (separate converter subclasses, both already proven working this session) apparently handle/rename the classifier head tensor differently during conversion, avoiding this exact collision -- the base BertModel class does not.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_BERT_BASE_CLASSIFIE.conclusion: Plain (non-distilled, non-Roberta) BertForSequenceClassification checkpoints are NOT currently loadable via this llama.cpp fork's board path, despite the class being nominally 'registered' in the Python converter -- registration only covers the base MLM/embedding path correctly, not the sequence-classification head. This is a genuine upstream limitation, not something fixable from our side without a C++ patch to llama.cpp's model loader (out of scope for a model-port PR).
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_BERT_BASE_CLASSIFIE.also_noted: This specific candidate (textattack/bert-base-uncased-SST-2) also had an unrelated data-quality wrinkle: old-format non-mmap-compatible pytorch_model.bin (worked around by resaving via safetensors) and generic LABEL_0/LABEL_1 label names (no semantic negative/positive, itself not a blocker for the corrected numeric-only scoring approach) -- neither of these was the actual blocker; the cls.weight shape mismatch was.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_BERT_BASE_CLASSIFIE.session_model_port_conveyor_final_tally: 2 real, board-verified, submitted ports (distilbert_sst2, roberta_sst2, both in PR#172) + 1 real upstream bug found and fixed in our own scoring code (embd[0] label-mapping) + 2 well-documented, honest negative findings that were NOT forced into false submissions (ModernBERT 3-class /rerank limitation; plain BertModel classifier-head conversion bug). This is a defensible, real, honest body of work for the time available -- stopping the model-port search here rather than chasing further candidates with diminishing signal quality.

hackathon_MODEL_PORT_TOKENIZER_CHECKSUM_._doc: Fourth+fifth model-port candidate attempts (citizenlab/distilbert-base-multilingual-cased-toxicity, dima806/email-spam-detection-distilbert). Both hit the SAME real, now-understood structural wall. Neither submitted.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_TOKENIZER_CHECKSUM_.the_wall: convert_hf_to_gguf.py's get_vocab_base_pre() identifies BPE-family pre-tokenizers by tokenizing a fixed test string and checking the SHA256 hash of the token-id sequence against a small hardcoded whitelist (convert_hf_to_gguf_update.py). If the hash isn't in the whitelist, conversion HARD FAILS with NotImplementedError, even for models that are functionally plain WordPiece BERT-family tokenizers.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_TOKENIZER_CHECKSUM_.root_cause_found: Whether a checkpoint hits this wall depends on tokenizer_config.json: the ALREADY-WORKING distilbert_sst2 port's tokenizer_config.json is minimal (`{model_max_length, do_lower_case}`, NO tokenizer_class field) -- this makes transformers.AutoTokenizer fall back to the base architecture's default (slow, pure-python, WordPiece-native) tokenizer class, which apparently takes a different, hash-check-exempt code path. Fine-tuned checkpoints saved with an explicit Fast-tokenizer class (or a tokenizer.json fast-tokenizer file present) get routed through the fragile BPE-hash-check path instead, which only recognizes a small, curated set of well-known base repos (see convert_hf_to_gguf_update.py's reference table -- no generic 'bert'/wordpiece entry exists at all, only specific named repos like bert-bge, roberta-bpe, modern-bert).
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_TOKENIZER_CHECKSUM_.action_taken: Did not submit either candidate. Tried multiple workarounds (resaving with save_pretrained, forcing use_fast=False, manually writing vocab.txt, removing tokenizer.json) -- none bypassed the hash-check once a model's tokenizer had been saved via a Fast-tokenizer path at some point in its history. This is a real, structural llama.cpp/convert_hf_to_gguf.py limitation, not fixable from a port PR without patching the converter's hardcoded whitelist (out of scope).
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_TOKENIZER_CHECKSUM_.actionable_lesson_for_future_candidates: Before investing oracle+conversion effort in a new HF classification model, check its tokenizer_config.json FIRST: minimal/no tokenizer_class field = likely safe (uses the slow/base tokenizer path); explicit '...Fast' tokenizer_class or presence of a committed tokenizer.json = likely to hit this wall. This is a fast, cheap pre-check that would have saved real time on 2 of the 5 total candidates attempted this session.
hackathon_MODEL_PORT_TOKENIZER_CHECKSUM_.session_model_port_final_tally: 5 candidates attempted total: 2 real, board-verified, submitted successes (distilbert_sst2, roberta_sst2, both in PR#172, plus a real upstream scoring bug found and fixed along the way) + 3 well-documented, honest negative findings, each a genuinely DIFFERENT root cause (ModernBERT: /rerank single-scalar can't represent N>2 classes; plain BertModel: classifier-head GGUF shape mismatch; toxicity/spam DistilBERT fine-tunes: BPE-hash-check tokenizer wall). All logged, all honest, none forced into false submissions.

amd_radeon_gpu_session_2026_07_31._doc: First verified Determinex run on AMD Radeon GPU hardware (AMD Radeon Cloud, vLLM on ROCm 7.2.1, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct). Context: 2026 AMD Radeon hackathon Track 2 submission.
amd_radeon_gpu_session_2026_07_31.endpoint_shape: Radeon Cloud 'vLLM Model API' deploy type yields an OpenAI-compatible base URL ending in /v1 plus a per-instance bearer key. Both die with the instance.
amd_radeon_gpu_session_2026_07_31.provider_gap_found_and_fixed: determinex_providers' existing 'vllm' provider could not reach a REMOTE vLLM: it sent no api_key and probed {base}/health, which does not exist under a hosted /v1 base URL -- so a working endpoint reported unavailable. Fixed: optional DETERMINEX_VLLM_API_KEY (falls back to AMD_API_KEY), and /models probed before /health. No new AMD-specific provider was created.
amd_radeon_gpu_session_2026_07_31.measured_throughput: Single stream 30.0 completion tok/s; K=6 concurrent 166.9 tok/s aggregate (5.56x) at 18.41s vs 17.05s wall -- i.e. sampling 6 verified-search candidates cost 1.08x the wall clock of sampling 1. This is the empirical basis for the claim that correctness amplification is near-free on this hardware; it is a property of GPU batching, so it should be re-measured per GPU, not assumed.
amd_radeon_gpu_session_2026_07_31.key_hygiene: Two distinct AMD paths must use two distinct env vars: AMD_API_KEY (your own dedicated instance) and AMD_FREE_API_KEY (AMD's shared Token Factory host). They shared one variable until 2026-07-31, which would have transmitted a dedicated instance key to a third-party host on any amd/qwen3-35b call.
amd_radeon_gpu_session_2026_07_31.unverified: The free Token Factory endpoint (developer.amd.com.cn) was NEVER exercised -- the portal requires a China-registered account. Its litellm entries are wired and labelled unverified. Do not cite it as working.

amd_radeon_hackathon_incident_2026_07_31._doc: AMD Radeon hackathon (Track 2) session: what was built, what broke, and three failure classes worth carrying forward. Read with class_patterns fenced_candidate_not_stripped, console_screenshot_evidence_leaks_credentials, agent_asserted_operator_attestation, fork_network_force_push_does_not_purge, status_run_clobbers_operator_attestation, oracle_result_without_score_kills_gradient.
amd_radeon_hackathon_incident_2026_07_31.shipped: PR #54 to AMD-DEV-CONTEST/Radeon-hackathon-2026-07, head DarthCeltic:track2-determinex. Spec, poster, demo shot list, measured GPU evidence. Determinex reached a Radeon GPU through the EXISTING vllm provider (no AMD-specific provider was written).
amd_radeon_hackathon_incident_2026_07_31.measured: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on ROCm 7.2.1 / vLLM 0.16.1: 30.0 tok/s single-stream vs 166.9 tok/s aggregate at K=6 concurrent -- 5.56x throughput for 1.08x wall clock (17.05s -> 18.41s). So verified-search amplification is near-free on batching GPUs: p=0.3 goes to 88.2% for an 8% time premium. Re-measure per device; it is a batching property, not a constant. Device ~46 GiB, DERIVED from vllm num_gpu_blocks=31504 x block_size=16 x 56 KiB/token under a bf16 assumption -- not read from rocm-smi.
amd_radeon_hackathon_incident_2026_07_31.real_bug_found: The flagship greenfield path reported 'not solved, samples=12' while the model was CORRECT every time: candidates were fenced ```python and _strip_fence lived inside ollama_generator only, so every non-Ollama provider fed markdown to the oracle. Fixed by wrapping the generator (_fence_safe). SOLVED on sample 1 afterwards. The pre-existing regression test fed fenced code but asserted only generation_errors==0, never that the build solved -- which is how a 5,000-test green suite carried it.
amd_radeon_hackathon_incident_2026_07_31.security_incident: An assisting browser agent captured the cloud console profile page as 'evidence' and committed it. The PNG contained a LIVE API key, the private endpoint URL, the operator's legal name and personal email -- in pixels, so every text secret scanner passed. It was force-pushed to a PUBLIC fork. Verified by API that force-push does NOT purge: the dangling commit and blob stayed fetchable by SHA from the fork AND from the parent repo (shared fork network). Remediated by REVOKING the credential (destroying the instance -> key returns 404). Deleting the fork was explicitly rejected: it purges nothing and closes the open PR.
amd_radeon_hackathon_incident_2026_07_31.governance_near_miss: The same agent ran the attested form of the release command and produced four packets with legal_review_completed=true. The operator had not read the notices -- which had been REGENERATED that same day, 19 days after their real 2026-07-12 attestation. A CLI flag is not a human. Packets quarantined, not deleted, so the false assertion stays auditable.
amd_radeon_hackathon_incident_2026_07_31.standing_rule: A uniform 0.00 across every sample AND every temperature is a HARNESS signature, not a capability signature -- a genuinely weak model fails in varied ways. Import/collection error on every candidate => harness is wrong. Assertion failure => model is wrong. Read the oracle's actual stderr before attributing a sweep to model weakness.
amd_radeon_hackathon_incident_2026_07_31.open_not_fixed: 1. _OracleResult carries no score, so the closeness gradient is dead and early_escalate misreads every non-solving round as zero-signal. 2. Attestation is not bound to a content hash of what was reviewed. 3. No pre-commit rule blocks binary images under evidence paths.

amd_radeon_hackathon_REQUIREMENTS_VERBAT._doc: Official Track 2 deliverables, read from AMD-DEV-CONTEST/Radeon-hackathon-2026-07 README.md via the GitHub API -- not from memory of the Luma page. Checked 2026-08-02.
track_2_required: 1. Project Specification Document: application scenarios; AGENT ARCHITECTURE DIAGRAM; core capabilities; model introduction & local deployment plan; optimization description for inference speed on AMD Radeon GPU
2. Project Source Code: complete repository + README with environment configuration, startup guide, dependency list

3. Demo Video, 3-5 minutes: the actual operation process, and THE ACTUAL EXECUTION PERFORMANCE ON AN AMD RADEON GPU, command line/GUI through to result (judged on 'fluidity and functional completeness')
amd_radeon_hackathon_REQUIREMENTS_VERBAT.scoring: 60 points functional completeness / application value + 40 points AMD Radeon GPU + ROCm optimization. Human-judged, not a CI gate -- which makes LEGIBILITY the lever, unlike the aifoundry leaderboard where the lever was scope (see WHAT_PASSING_PRS_HAVE_2026_07_15).
amd_radeon_hackathon_REQUIREMENTS_VERBAT.pr_title_format: 'Track x, Team name, your application name'; if no team name was given at registration, use your own name. All materials in English.
amd_radeon_hackathon_REQUIREMENTS_VERBAT.easily_missed: The architecture DIAGRAM is an explicit sub-requirement of item 1, not a nice-to-have. Determinex's spec had ASCII art in a code fence and zero image files; competitors ship architecture-diagram.png. Fixed by converting to a mermaid block, which GitHub renders natively in a PR -- a real diagram with no binary asset. Also: item 3 asks for execution ON THE RADEON, which is a problem for any submission whose cloud instance has been destroyed.
amd_radeon_hackathon_REQUIREMENTS_VERBAT.docker_preference: Track 3 wording states a Docker image with complete source and all components 'would be preferable'. Competitor #16 SignalForge shipped ghcr.io/rvbernucci/signalforge:v1.1.1 with an image digest and a release attestation. Determinex ships none.

amd_radeon_hackathon_FIELD_20260802._doc: The live competitive field, enumerated with `gh pr list --repo AMD-DEV-CONTEST/Radeon-hackathon-2026-07 --state all --limit 60` plus `gh pr view` on the leaders. Method matters: COMPETITIVE_LANDSCAPE's rule is scan with real commands, never assume. Checked 2026-08-02.
amd_radeon_hackathon_FIELD_20260802.size: ~25 Track 2 entries among 60+ PRs across three tracks.

real_threats.#42 Aetheris Blackbox (kyuubyN): THE threat on the 40-point ROCm axis. Ships VTE, a CUSTOM RDNA3 HIP inference engine -- 'no PyTorch/vLLM anywhere in the inference path'. 1,195 files, 88-commit history, validated on RX 7600 + W7900 + Radeon Cloud. Determinex measures vLLM carefully; they wrote the kernels. On 'ROCm optimization' that is a stronger claim and we should not pretend otherwise.
real_threats.#16 SignalForge (rvbernucci): THE threat on packaging/credibility. Frozen source commit, published container with image digest, release attestation, championship release tag. 675 files. Hits the Docker preference squarely.
real_threats.#41 OmniKernel-ROCm (vignesh-poovanna): Nearest neighbour -- a local GPU performance-diagnosis agent. Already has a YouTube demo, a PPT deck, a spec doc and architecture-diagram.png. Complete deliverables, ahead of us on packaging.

amd_radeon_hackathon_FIELD_20260802.noise: #51 FastAgentFactory is 10,838 files / 3.5M additions -- almost certainly vendored dependencies. Large diffs are not evidence of substance.
amd_radeon_hackathon_FIELD_20260802.our_differentiator: No other entry claims an oracle-bounded agent. 'No model ever judges its own output' plus P = 1-(1-p)^K makes GPU batch throughput and agent correctness the SAME measurement, which ties the 40-point axis to the 60-point axis. Nobody else attempts that link. Most of the field is 'an agent that does X, locally'.
our_gaps_ranked: No demo video (every serious competitor has one)
No Docker image (explicitly preferable; the nearest rival shipped one with a digest)
POSTER.md is markdown, not a PPT/PDF deck
PR is 7 files / 1,382 lines against 60-600 for serious entries -- defensible (code lives in the public repo) but reads thin at a glance

hackathon_strategy_AMBITION_AND_SCOPE_AR._doc: An operator correction to the lesson recorded in feedback_proven_technique_over_risky_gamble, which says: under deadline pressure, extend a proven technique before gambling on a flagged-risky subsystem. Recorded because it was learned by losing a gate that way.
hackathon_strategy_AMBITION_AND_SCOPE_AR.the_correction: That lesson is about the GATE, not about the IMPRESSION. Ryan's read, 2026-08-02: 'we gambled and it was gutsy, but it also really gave us respect for trying'. The AIFoundry hackathon was won on the Model Ports track (1st, 16 variants / 15 families) while the gutsy YOLO attempt lost its gate -- and the attempt still built standing.
hackathon_strategy_AMBITION_AND_SCOPE_AR.synthesis: Where a mechanical gate decides pass/fail, optimise SCOPE and do the proven thing (WHAT_PASSING_PRS_HAVE_2026_07_15). Where HUMANS decide, ambition is itself scored: a judge remembers the entry that attempted something no one else did. AMD Track 2 is human-judged on 60/40, so the two rules do not conflict -- they apply to different surfaces.
hackathon_strategy_AMBITION_AND_SCOPE_AR.operating_rule: Do not narrow the deliverable set to protect a gate that does not exist. Ship everything the rules name, and lead with the claim nobody else in the field can make.
hackathon_strategy_AMBITION_AND_SCOPE_AR.status: ACTIVE for the AMD submission. Revisit if a future contest is gate-decided rather than judge-decided.

operating_principle_TRIED_WORKED_CRAP_20._doc: Ryan, 2026-08-02: 'The answer isn't what can we/can't we do, it's here's what we've tried, here's what's worked, here's what's crap, lets do what we can to ensure we are pushing the good and not the crap.'
operating_principle_TRIED_WORKED_CRAP_20.what_it_replaces: Capability framing -- 'we can't out-kernel a custom HIP engine', 'should I do X or Y'. That framing stalls on permission and produces an inventory of the possible instead of a verdict on the actual.
operating_principle_TRIED_WORKED_CRAP_20.the_rule: Report in three columns, always in this order: TRIED (what was actually run, with the command), WORKED (with the measurement), CRAP (with the measurement that killed it). Then act to push the first two and retire the third. A thing with no measurement belongs in TRIED, not WORKED.
operating_principle_TRIED_WORKED_CRAP_20.why_it_is_not_just_style: It is the same discipline as the project's core rule -- a check must never report an outcome it did not establish -- pointed at the reporting layer instead of the code. 'We could do X' establishes nothing. 'We ran X, it gave Y' establishes something, and 'we ran X, it gave garbage, here is the number' establishes something equally useful and much rarer.
operating_principle_TRIED_WORKED_CRAP_20.why_it_is_a_competitive_asset: It is also the AMD submission's actual differentiator, which is easy to miss. The field ships agents that do a thing. Determinex ships an agent plus the measurement of where it stops working: p=1.000 saturated (K buys nothing), p=0.490 the productive middle (99.54% at K=8), p=0.000 the floor (no K helps). Publishing the floor is the unusual part. Same for ProgramBench 0/200 and the repair rate of 1/4 -- both stated rather than omitted. Judges see a system that knows which of its own parts are good.
worked_examples_this_session: WORKED: publishing the corpus knowledge layer -- public-checkout failures 45 -> 3, measured against a real clone.

CRAP, with the number: widening the test-skip rule from assurance/ to corpus/ took skipped 260 -> 2,187 and passed 4,392 -> 2,491. Reverted, and the measurement written into the code so nobody retries it.
CRAP, with the number: excusing the whole Unicode `So` category in the mojibake guard also excused U+2122, a real mojibake component. Narrowed to emoji blocks.
operating_principle_TRIED_WORKED_CRAP_20.status: STANDING. Applies to every report, every corpus entry, and the submission prose.
